# crew — agent orientation

This project runs [crew](https://github.com/brianmmorton/crew): an autonomous
team of role-specialized coding agents that read and write to this directory.
If you are an agent (or a human) trying to understand what's here, this file
is the map.

## What crew does

crew runs a small team of agents against one repo:

- **Proposers** (`qa`, `architect`, `design`, ...) are read-only. On a cron
  cadence, each reads the repo and/or its granted MCP tools and files typed
  work items (`bug` / `task` / `chore-dx` / `spike` / `prd`) into the issue
  tracker (Linear or Jira).
- **The implementer** (the default executor) claims one ready work item at a
  time, implements it in an isolated git worktree, and opens a PR. Custom
  executors can claim a subset of work by label instead.
- **Reviewers** run after a PR opens, leave comments, and — only if
  explicitly allowed — move the issue to a listed workflow state.
- Anything crew judges **material** (see `constitution.md`) is gated behind a
  PRD that a human must approve before any code is written. Everything else
  flows straight from proposal to implementation.

Agents are **stateless workers**: they return typed proposals, commit
outcomes, or review verdicts, and the engine (not the agent) performs every
tracker mutation, git operation, and PR action deterministically. This is why
an MCP server that can write to the tracker directly is refused at config
validation — it would let a persona route around dedup, the proposal caps,
and the PRD approval gate.

## Directory layout

| File | Owner | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `config.yaml` | you | All settings — see below. Committed; never holds secrets. |
| `constitution.md` | you | What counts as "material" for THIS project — the PRD gate's policy. |
| `personas/*.md` | you | One agent per file: its prompt, plus optional frontmatter settings. |
| `.env` | you, gitignored | Real secret values for the `${VAR}` placeholders in `config.yaml`. |
| `.env.example` | crew | Template listing which secrets each provider needs. |
| `AGENTS.md` | crew | This file. Regenerated on upgrade — don't hand-edit. |
| `state.json` | crew, runtime | Supervisor pid, last-run timestamps, retry counters. Don't edit. |

Add a new agent with `crew agent new <name>` or `crew agent add` (the
conversational version), or just drop a `.md` file into `personas/` — it's
discovered automatically.

## `config.yaml` field reference

Every field below is real — this list is kept in sync with the config
schema, so nothing here is aspirational. The scaffolded `config.yaml` in this
directory has all of these as either live settings or commented-out examples;
uncomment what you need.

- **`project`** — a name for logging and the TUI header.
- **`repo.path`** — defaults to `.` (the git toplevel containing this dir).
  **`repo.baseBranch`** — defaults to `main`. **`repo.forge`** — `github`
  (via the `gh` CLI) or `bitbucket` (Cloud REST API). **`repo.bitbucketRepo`**
  — `"workspace/repo-slug"`, inferred from the origin remote if omitted.
- **`agent.provider`** — `"claude"` is the built-in adapter (streaming +
  subscription auth via `claude`). Any other value drives an external CLI
  through **`agent.command`**, **`agent.args`**, **`agent.promptVia`**
  (`"stdin"` or `"arg"`), **`agent.modelFlag`**, **`agent.mcpConfigFlag`**,
  **`agent.mcpStrictFlag`**.
- **`mcpServers.<name>`** — external tool servers, granted to personas by
  name via `personas.<name>.mcp`. Never inherited from your own Claude
  Code/Codex config — grants are always explicit. Transport is implied by
  shape: **`command`** (+ **`args`**, **`env`**) is stdio; **`url`** (+
  **`type`**: `"http"`/`"sse"`, **`headers`**) is HTTP/SSE. **`oauth`** (see
  below) is for servers requiring OAuth instead of a static header token.
  **`allowedTools`** is advisory only — headless runs skip the CLI
  permission system entirely, so this is injected into the prompt as an
  instruction, not enforced. **`description`** is a one-line note shown in
  `crew agents`/`crew doctor`. Secrets go in `${VAR}` placeholders, resolved
  from `.env`/`~/.crew/env` at spawn time into a temp file outside the repo.
- **`mcpServers.<name>.oauth`** — **`authorizationUrl`**, **`tokenUrl`**,
  **`clientId`**, optional **`clientSecret`** (confidential clients only),
  optional **`scopes`**, optional **`redirectUri`** (only if the provider
  needs a pre-registered exact redirect). Run `crew mcp login <name>` once
  per machine to authorize interactively (opens a browser); after that crew
  refreshes the access token itself before every run, headless or not.
  `crew mcp status` / `crew mcp logout <name>` manage the stored token
  (`~/.crew/oauth/<name>.json`, mode 0600). A refresh failure skips that
  persona's run with a message naming the server, rather than failing
  silently or crashing the cycle.
- **`tracker.provider`** — `"linear"` or `"jira"` (the old `linear:` top-level
  spelling still parses the same way). **`tracker.team`** — a Linear team
  name or Jira project key. **`tracker.project`** — optional scoping below
  the team (a Linear project or Jira component), so several repos can share
  one team/project. **`tracker.labels.{prd,bug,task,chore,stuck,needsHuman}`**
  — the type/state labels crew applies; `stuck`/`needsHuman` are
  engine-managed, not meant to be hand-set. **`tracker.statuses.*`** —
  workflow state names, exactly as they appear on your board.
  **`tracker.approvedStates`** — states that count as "not blocked."
  **`tracker.executable.requireLabels`** / **`excludeLabels`** — gate what
  the executor may *claim* out of ready (empty = everything is fair game).
  **`tracker.autoPromote`** — non-material proposals go straight to ready
  when true (default); set false to stage everything in Backlog for manual
  promotion. **`tracker.jira.issueTypes.*`**, **`subtaskIssueType`**,
  **`usePriority`**, **`priorities.*`** — Jira-only, ignored on Linear.
- **`budget.target`** — `"max-monthly"` or `"fixed"`. **`implementerWorkers`**
  — parallel implementer slots (1–8). **`backoffMinutes`**, **`pollSeconds`**.
- **`worktrees.reuse`** — off by default (fresh worktree every cycle, proven
  cold). Set true on a large repo where a cold checkout + `gates.setup` costs
  real time per cycle. **`max`** — pool size, defaults to
  `budget.implementerWorkers`. **`preserveArtifacts`** — untracked-but-not-
  gitignored paths a reset keeps (the one setting here that can produce a
  *wrong* result, not just a slow one, if you list a build output rather
  than a cache). **`recycleAfter`** — force a full clean every N reuses (0 =
  never).
- **`gates.wipCap`** — max items in flight at once. **`gates.setup`** — shell
  command to prep the env before verify (activate a runtime, install deps).
  **`gates.verify`** — map of app name → command; empty means trust the
  agent + PR review with no automated gate. **`gates.noTouch`** — globs the
  implementer must never modify.
- **`models.default`** — empty uses Claude Code's own default.
  **`models.byComplexity.{low,medium,high}`** — maps a work item's
  `complexity` label to a model; prefer short aliases (`haiku`, `sonnet`,
  `opus`, `best`, `opusplan`) so they auto-track the latest version.
- **`personas.<name>`** — per-agent overrides (same fields can live as
  frontmatter in `personas/<name>.md`; this block wins on conflict).
  **`kind`** (`proposer`/`executor`/`reviewer`), **`cadence`** (cron;
  proposers only), **`model`**, **`description`**, **`allowedTypes`** (item
  types this agent may file), **`maxProposals`** (cap per run), **`label`**
  (extra tracker label on everything it files), **`claims`** (labels an
  executor claims; unclaimed work falls to `implementer`),
  **`canTransitionTo`** (workflow states a reviewer may move an issue to —
  empty means comment-only), **`mcp`** (server names to grant, from
  `mcpServers` above).
- **`triager.cadence`**, **`dedupThreshold`** (similarity above which a new
  proposal is treated as a duplicate), **`backlogCap`**,
  **`dedupLookbackDays`** (how long a *completed* item keeps blocking a
  near-duplicate; canceled items block forever).
- **`idle.enabled`** — pull a proposer in early when the executor has no
  work, instead of waiting for its next cron tick. **`afterMinutes`** — how
  long the queue must be empty first. **`minIntervalMinutes`** — floor on
  how often any one proposer runs, across cron *and* idle triggers.
  **`maxBacklog`** — skip idle triggers while the backlog is already this
  deep. **`maxEmptyRuns`** — stop triggering after this many idle runs file
  nothing (resumes once the board changes). **`agents`** — which proposers
  idle may pull in; empty = all of them.
- **`ui.logoUrl`** — optional image URL rendered as ASCII art in the TUI
  header/splash in place of the "crew" wordmark.

The `.crew/` directory name itself can be overridden with the `CREW_DIR` env
var, and which repo commands target with `CREW_REPO` — both useful when
driving a sibling repo without `cd`-ing into it.

## Commands you'll use most

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `crew doctor` | Check required tools/secrets/OAuth logins are present |
| `crew status` | Backlog / WIP counts, schedule, in-flight work |
| `crew agents` | List every agent, its kind, cadence, options |
| `crew once <agent>` | Run one cycle of any agent right now |
| `crew` | Run the whole team on a live screen: executor loop + scheduled proposers |
| `crew mcp login/logout/status <server>` | Manage OAuth for MCP servers |
| `crew probe` | Prove `gates.setup`/`gates.verify` pass in a cold worktree |

## Safety model, in one paragraph

Agents propose; the engine decides. Dedup, `allowedTypes`, `maxProposals`,
and the PRD approval gate all live in the engine, not in any agent — which is
also why a granted MCP server that can write to the tracker directly is
refused at validation. `allowedTools` on an MCP grant is documentation, not
enforcement (headless runs skip the CLI's permission system). The two
controls that actually hold are **which servers a persona is granted at
all**, and **the scope of the token you issue it** — grant read-only servers
read-only tokens.
